1.visual: A pair of curly braces — an opening brace on the left and a closing brace on the right — the code block delimiter symbol.
1.usage: code block indicator, JSON editor, template expression wrapper, programming syntax reference

2.visual: A beetle-like bug viewed from above with a rounded body, two antennae, and three pairs of legs on each side.
2.usage: bug report, issue tracker, debug mode toggle, error log viewer

3.visual: A less-than chevron on the left and a greater-than chevron on the right, pointing outward — the HTML tag or code embed symbol.
3.usage: source code view, HTML/XML editor, embed content, developer mode toggle

4.visual: Four small squares each rotated 45 degrees into a diamond shape, arranged in a 2x2 grid pattern.
4.usage: app grid launcher, component library overview, widget gallery, dashboard tiles

5.visual: A 3D isometric box viewed from above-left with vertical dividing lines on its front face, resembling a partitioned container.
5.usage: package manager, Docker container, build artifact, software bundle

6.visual: A cylinder with two horizontal bands dividing it into three stacked sections — the classic database storage symbol.
6.usage: database connection, data storage, SQL interface, backend data source

7.visual: A database cylinder with a curved counterclockwise arrow wrapping around its lower-right base, indicating restore or rollback.
7.usage: database restore, rollback migration, backup recovery, revert database state

8.visual: A plus sign stacked directly above a minus sign, the plus-minus mathematical symbol.
8.usage: code diff view, added and removed lines indicator, version delta, numeric tolerance

9.visual: Two small circles — one at the top of a vertical stem and one at the bottom-right — connected by a curved arc, a git branch diagram.
9.usage: git branch, create new branch, version control branch view, branching workflow

10.visual: A horizontal line with a small hollow circle (ring) centered on it — the git commit node on a timeline.
10.usage: git commit marker, single commit view, commit history, version checkpoint

11.visual: Two circles connected by an L-shaped path — one circle at upper-left and one at lower-right — suggesting a two-node branch path.
11.usage: git diff, compare branches, code review selector, pull request source and target

12.visual: Three circles in a fork layout — one at the top center branching down to two at bottom-left and bottom-right — a git fork diagram.
12.usage: fork repository, git network graph, repository fork indicator, branch divergence

13.visual: Two parallel vertical lines each capped with a circle at top and bottom, side by side — resembling a git pull request with two branch endpoints.
13.usage: pull request view, open PR indicator, parallel branch display, branch management

14.visual: Two circles joined by a smooth curved arc — one at top-left and one at bottom-right — meeting at a single converging path, a git merge symbol.
14.usage: git merge, merge branch, merge request, combine branch into main

15.visual: A circle at top-left with a vertical stem connected via a right-angle path to a second circle at lower-right with its own stem — forming a bracket-like shape between two branch endpoints.
15.usage: git stash, shelve changes, save work in progress, temporary branch storage

16.visual: A filled circle at top-left with a vertical stem, next to a second circle at lower-right marked with an X above it — indicating a closed or rejected branch.
16.usage: closed pull request, rejected branch, cancelled merge, deleted branch indicator

17.visual: A filled circle at top-left with a vertical stem, next to a hollow ring circle at lower-right with two small dots beside it — suggesting a draft or pending branch state.
17.usage: draft pull request, work-in-progress branch, pending review status, unfinished PR

18.visual: Three rows each showing a small filled dot bullet on the left with a short horizontal line extending to the right — a bullet list.
18.usage: list view, changelog, task list, unordered list items

19.visual: A jigsaw puzzle piece with convex tabs and concave notches on all four sides, able to interlock from any direction.
19.usage: plugin system, extension or add-on, integration panel, modular feature

20.visual: A small hollow square at lower-left paired with a large asterisk at upper-right — the regex or wildcard pattern symbol.
20.usage: regular expression toggle, wildcard search, glob pattern input, regex mode activation

21.visual: A magnifying glass with a pair of angle bracket chevrons (less-than and greater-than) displayed inside its lens.
21.usage: code search, find in source, search symbols or functions, inspect element

22.visual: A right-pointing chevron followed by a short horizontal dash to its right — the terminal command prompt symbol.
22.usage: terminal panel, CLI launcher, shell command prompt, developer console or REPL

23.visual: An X character flanked by a left parenthesis on the left and a right parenthesis on the right, forming the expression (x).
23.usage: function parameter, math expression editor, variable binding, remove or clear formula

24.visual: A continuous looping line forming three rounded arches joined end-to-end in a triangular closed loop — a webhook symbol.
24.usage: webhook configuration, HTTP callback setup, event trigger, automation listener

25.visual: Two rounded squares connected by a short diagonal line, with one square at upper-left and a smaller one at lower-right.
25.usage: dependency link, connected components, linked modules, relational data indicator
